validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via multiple independent, non-GEM sources across 3 decades of coverage, not a GEM-only entity. (1) 'Sostoyanie i perspektivy razvitiya transporta nefti i gaza Kazakhstana', Neft i Gaz journal, March 2019 (neft-gas.kz PDF, verified live+downloaded, pdftotext -layout confirms text at p.98): lists 'Zhanaozen-Aktau' among Kazakhstan's operating trunk gas pipelines, capacity 3.6 bcm/y (pre-modernization baseline), length 427 km (whole multi-string system), operator listed as JSC KTG-Aimak. (2) Intergas Central Asia's own 2023 Annual Report (PDF verified live, pdftotext -layout p.21/28): lists MG 'Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau' as one of the trunk lines under its UMG Aktau (Administration of Trunk Gas Pipelines) branch, alongside Beineu-Bozoy-Shymkent and KazGPZ-KS-Zhanaozen, and describes a completed capital-repair project on '3 strings of MG Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau' that raised max pressure 2.7->5.4 MPa and MG throughput capacity 2.68->4.54 bcm/y. (3) Turantimes.kz Feb 2023 (verified live) and Intergas's own Feb 2023 news item (verified live, https://intergas.kz/ru/news/4/991, article text confirms 282-pipe replacement, 14 bn tenge, ~85% complete Feb 2023, planned completion Sept 2023): independently corroborate a live, ongoing capital-repair + a separate NEW 4th-string construction project on this exact corridor. (4) INAktau.kz local news (undated, ~2023-24, verified live): independently (non-Intergas) states the pre-repair max capacity of MG 'Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau' was 2.68 bn m3 (matching the Intergas AR's 'before' figure exactly) and gives the pipe diameter as '529/530 mm' for this line, plus separately confirms the 4th-string construction (contractor Trans Asia Construction, 46 km laid by article date, completion targeted 2025). This is a real, actively-maintained multi-string trunk system, not a hallucination. CLASSIFICATION: every source calls it a 'magistralny gazoprovod' (MG, trunk gas pipeline) -- consistent with GEM's PipelineType=transmission; no basis to reclassify. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the roster's flagged P5784: NOT a duplicate. The roster's one-line summary shows P5784 as 'Zhetybay->Mangistau' which looks identical to P5783, but the worklist's own segment_name for P5784 is 'Zhetybay-Kuryk Branch Gas Pipeline' -- a different destination (Kuryk, not Aktau). This is independently corroborated by a wiki-cited QazaqGaz 2023 press release, 'Stroitelstvo MG Zhetybay-Kuryk s ustanovkoy AGRS-80 v s.Kuryk', announcing NEW construction of a Zhetybay-Kuryk branch with an AGRS-80 gas distribution station in the Kuryk settlement -- a distinct physical corridor. The roster's apparent overlap is a labeling artifact of the country-notes summary, not a real duplicate; the length/diameter similarity (70.8 vs 70.0 km, 529 vs 530 mm) is coincidental parallel-pipe-class sizing, not evidence of double-counting. Structural note (not a P5783 defect, flagging for the cluster): P5783 (70.8 km, 'III Zhetybay-Aktau') + P5777 (60.7 km, 'III Zhanaozen-Zhetybay') = 131.4 km, the full end-to-end length of String III. P3948 ('I', full Uzen->Mangistau, 149.1 km) is suspiciously close to P5776+P5777+P5783 combined (17.8+60.7+70.8=149.3 km) -- worth a separate look at whether P3948 is double-counting the sum of Strings II+III rather than being its own independent String I, but that concern belongs to P3948's own shard, not P5783's. ATTRIBUTION -- genuine open question, see separate validity entry below on Operator. SPEC: Diameter 529 mm independently corroborated (INAktau gives '529/530 mm' for this exact line). Capacity 4.54 bcm/y is the correct POST-2023-repair figure per Intergas's own AR, with the pre-repair baseline (2.68) independently corroborated by INAktau -- tier medium, since only one strong primary source states the final 4.54 figure directly (Intergas AR), though a second independent outlet corroborates the underlying repair project and its 'before' number. Length 70.80 km could NOT be independently corroborated at the per-segment ('Zhetybay-Aktau' specifically) level in any source found -- all located sources describe the trunk system in aggregate (whole-system 427 km in 2019) or give diameters/capacities, not a Zhetybay-Aktau-specific length; leaving as-is, unresolved at segment granularity, not contradicted either. StartYear1=1968 is plausible (Uzen/Zhetybay oil-and-gas field development began mid-1960s; a nearby 'hot' oil pipeline Uzen-Shevchenko was commissioned 1966 per the 2019 Neft i Gaz article) but no source names 1968 specifically for this gas line -- leaving as-is, unresolved.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Operator field is 'АО «КазТрансГаз Аймак»' (KazTransGaz Aimak), supported by a 2019 Neft i Gaz journal article which explicitly names 'АО «КТГ-Аймак»' as operator of 'Zhanaozen-Aktau'. However, Intergas Central Asia's OWN 2023 Annual Report (verified live PDF) lists 'MG Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau' as part of ITS OWN network under its 'UMG Aktau' (Administration of Trunk Gas Pipelines, Aktau branch), and describes performing a capital-repair project directly on this line as ITS OWN completed 2023 project. Independently, INAktau.kz's local news article states verbatim: 'Ostanovimsya na proektakh, provodimykh upravleniem magistralnykh gazoprovodov AO Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya. Proekt Kapitalny remont magistralnogo gazoprovoda Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau...' -- i.e. it was Intergas Central Asia's own Administration of Trunk Gas Pipelines that commissioned/managed the capital repair (using contractor TOO 'Kagam' for construction work), not KazTransGaz Aimak. This is a genuine conflict between an older (2019) source naming KTG-Aimak and two more recent (2023-24) sources -- one of them independent of Intergas -- showing Intergas Central Asia as the active operator/manager of this exact trunk line. Plausible explanation: KazTransGaz Aimak (a regional GAS DISTRIBUTION subsidiary) may have operated the line pre-2019/pre-QazaqGaz-spinoff (Nov 2021), with trunk-transmission operatorship since consolidated under Intergas Central Asia -- but this is inference, not confirmed fact. Given GEM's row was last updated 2024-08-23, after both 2023-24 sources, the Operator value may be stale. Not applying any change here (per standing rules, only flagging); routing to Update.

summary: P5783 exists and is correctly classified as a real, actively-repaired trunk-pipeline string (verdict confirmed (caveat)); diameter 529mm and capacity 4.54 bcm/y (post-2023-repair) independently corroborated at medium tier; NOT a duplicate of P5784 (that row is a separate Zhetybay-Kuryk branch, not Zhetybay-Aktau); one genuine attribution concern staged -- Operator may be stale (KazTransGaz Aimak vs. Intergas Central Asia, which 2023-24 sources show actively managing this line); length 70.80 km and StartYear 1968 remain UNRESOLVED (unconfirmed at segment level, not contradicted).
